messages:
sam_sales: Heads up — Acme POC seeing repeated 429s during embeddings demo. Customer running batched embed jobs (50 reqs/s peak) and hitting errors after ~30s. Can we triage? :eyes:

maria_eng: Can you paste a sample request_id + route? and approximate token sizes for the batch?

sam_sales: request_id=01H8J3QZ5, route=/v1/embeddings, tokens ~120 per doc, batch sizes of 16 in parallel. Getting a lot of `429` responses. No obvious 5xx.

olivia_support: Logged the request_id, I see the 429s in the logs: `status=429 x-rate-limit-remaining=0 x-route-cap=60/min`. Looks like per-route cap and global burst interacting.

lee_backend: Quick hypothesis — per-route cap (60/min) + per-tenant token budget is being hit because parallel batches multiply token accounting. If each embedding counts as token units, the token-bucket drains fast.

devon_sre: Can you paste the exact headers from one failed response? also run `curl -I https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -H 'X-Request-Id: 01H8J3QZ5'` to capture rate headers.

sam_sales: Paste from customer (redacted):
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
X-Request-Id: 01H8J3QZ5
X-Rate-Limit-Limit: 60
X-Rate-Limit-Remaining: 0
X-Rate-Limit-Reset: 2026-05-03T16:23:40Z
X-Route-Cap: embeddings=60/min
{"error":{"message":"rate limit exceeded"}}
```

maria_eng: That X-Route-Cap line looks like the static per-route cap. The POC was configured with default per-route caps. For embedding-heavy demos we usually recommend bumping per-route to 300/min or using batching settings to reduce parallelism.

sam_sales: The customer asked for a quick workaround during the demo window. Can we do a temporary per-route increase?

quota-admin-bot: @olivia_support requested a temporary per-route cap increase for tenant `acme-corp` on route `/v1/embeddings` from 60/min to 300/min for 2 hours — pending approval.

devon_sre: Before approving, let's confirm token-accounting: are we charging per input token or per embedding vector? If per-input tokens, 16 parallel * 120 tokens * 50 reqs/s is huge. We might need to advise client to reduce parallel batches or enable client-side batching.

olivia_support: Confirmed: accounting is per input token for embedding calls. I pushed the approval for a 2-hour bump; ops will apply it in ~2 min.

lee_backend: Also recommend turning on `client_batching=true` in their SDK (docs: https://docs.redwood.ai/embeddings#batching). That will coalesce small requests into fewer server-side ops and smooth the token burn.

sam_sales: Ops applied the bump, can someone ask the customer to retry?

maria_eng: Also adding a short-term mitigation: enable linear backoff on 429 with jitter (base=200ms, cap=3s) and throttle parallelism to 8 concurrent batches.

[some minutes later]
sam_sales: Customer retried — initial results: success, 429s dropped to near zero. demo continuing. :tada:

devon_sre: Follow-up items: 1) add a per-route recommendations note to the sales POC checklist (embeddings default should show recommended caps for common demo patterns), 2) add an automated hint in the dashboard when x-route-cap is low for a tenant doing heavy embedding ops.

olivia_support: Captured runbook steps and added a KB: "POC embeddings burst -> check X-Route-Cap -> temp bump -> advise batching/backoff". Link: https://kb.redwood.ai/poc-embeddings-rate-bumps

sam_sales: Thanks team — customer is unblocked for the rest of the demo. Leaving thread so we can follow up on checklist and docs updates.

maria_eng: I'll open a short PR for the sales checklist and add a tooltip in the console about per-route caps.

lee_backend: We should also expose per-tenant token burn charts in the Console to make suspicious bursts obvious earlier.

devon_sre: Good. Marking this resolved for now, re-open if 429s resurface.

sam_sales: Closing — will follow up with ACME post-demo to recommend production config. :white_check_mark:
